cohort: Adult patients who received either an -80 mm Hg or -125 mm Hg single-use negative pressure wound therapy device after a cesarean delivery.
finding: Use of the -80 mm Hg sNPWT device was associated with a lower likelihood of developing overall SSI, superficial SSI, dehiscence, and seroma, as well as lower costs, compared to the -125 mm Hg device after cesarean delivery.
